questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct about the gravitational force between the earth and the moon?

options.text: Gravitational force is repulsive when the moon is far from the earth.
Gravitational force is repulsive and minimum when the moon is far from the earth.
Gravitational force is attractive and maximum when the moon is close to the earth.
Gravitational force is attractive and maximum when the moon is far from the earth.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gravitational force is attractive and maximum when the moon is close to the earth.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The gravitational force between two objects is always attractive in nature.
 
• The force of gravity is directly proportional to the product of the masses of the two objects involved.
 
• It is inversely proportional to the square of the distance between the centers of the two objects.
 
• As the distance between the moon and the earth decreases, the gravitational force between them increases.
 
• When the moon is closest to the earth, the gravitational force is at its maximum value.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Inverse Square Law**

 
 
• The gravitational force follows the inverse square law, meaning it decreases with the square of the distance between the two objects.
 
 
 
• **Newton's Law of Universal Gravitation**
 
 
• This law states that every point mass attracts every other point mass by a force acting along the line intersecting both points.
 
 
 
• **Tidal Forces**
 
 
• The gravitational attraction between the earth and moon causes tidal forces, which are responsible for the ocean tides on earth.

questions.question: The equivalent resistance of the combination of resistors, when 1 ohm and 2 ohm are connected in parallel, is _____.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Resistors: 1 ohm and 2 ohm connected in parallel.

**Concept Used:**

For resistors in parallel, the equivalent resistance (Rₑq) is given by:

1/Rₑq = 1/R₁ + 1/R₂

**Calculation:**

We have,

⇒ R₁ = 1 ohm, R₂ = 2 ohm

⇒ 1/Rₑq = 1/1 + 1/2

⇒ 1/Rₑq = 1 + 1/2

⇒ 1/Rₑq = (2 + 1)/2

⇒ 1/Rₑq = 3/2

⇒ Rₑq = 2/3 ohm

**∴ The equivalent resistance is 2/3 ohm.**

questions.question: Average velocity of a body can be given by the arithmetic mean of initial velocity and final velocity for a given period of time when the body is:
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**moving with uniform acceleration**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Average velocity** is calculated as the arithmetic mean of the **initial velocity** and **final velocity** when the body is moving under **uniform acceleration**.
 
• This is because under **uniform acceleration**, the change in velocity is linear and equally distributed over time.
 
• The formula for average velocity in this case is: **(Initial velocity + Final velocity) / 2**.
 
• Uniform acceleration implies that the rate of change of velocity is constant during the given period of time.
 
• This relationship holds true for motion in a straight line, such as a body falling under the influence of **gravity** (ignoring air resistance).
 
• For example, in cases like the motion of a car accelerating uniformly or free-fall motion, this method of calculating average velocity can be applied.
 
• If the acceleration is not uniform, this formula does not apply, and the average velocity must be calculated by integrating the velocity function over time.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Moving with non-uniform acceleration**__

 __
 
• **Non-uniform acceleration** refers to a situation where the rate of change of velocity is not constant.
 
• In this case, the velocity changes irregularly over time, and the average velocity cannot be determined using the simple arithmetic mean formula.
 
• Instead, the average velocity must be calculated by integrating the velocity function over the time interval.
 
 
 
• **Moving with uniform speed**__
 __
 
• **Uniform speed** implies that the body covers equal distances in equal intervals of time.
 
• In this case, the average velocity is the same as the constant speed, and there is no variation in velocity to consider.
 
 
 
• **Moving with uniform velocity**__
 
 
• **Uniform velocity** means that both the speed and direction of motion remain constant throughout the period of time.
 
• Since there is no change in velocity, the initial velocity equals the final velocity, and the average velocity will be the same as the constant velocity.

questions.question: If x : y = 7: 3, then ( x - y ) : ( x + y ) = ?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

x : y = 7 : 3

**Formula Used:**

(x - y) : (x + y)

**Calculation:**

Let x = 7k and y = 3k

x - y = 7k - 3k = 4k

x + y = 7k + 3k = 10k

(x - y) : (x + y) = 4k : 10k

Divide both sides by k:

4 : 10

Simplify by dividing both sides by 2:

4 / 2 : 10 / 2

2 : 5

**Therefore, (x - y) : (x + y) = 2 : 5.**

questions.question: After a decrease of 24%, the price of an article is ₹988. The actual cost of the article is:

Final price after decrease = x - (24/100) × x = ₹988

⇒ x = 988 / 0.76

questions.question: The area of the base of a rectangular tank is 6500 cm² and the volume of water contained in it is 2.6 cubic meters. The depth of water in the tank is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Area of the base of a rectangular tank = 6500 cm²

Volume of water contained in the tank = 2.6 cubic meters

**Formula Used:**

Volume = Area × Depth

**Calculation:**

First, convert the volume from cubic meters to cubic centimeters:

1 cubic meter = 1,000,000 cubic centimeters

Therefore, 2.6 cubic meters = 2.6 × 1,000,000 = 2,600,000 cm³

Using the formula:

Volume = Area × Depth

⇒ Depth = Volume / Area

⇒ Depth = 2,600,000 cm³ / 6500 cm²

⇒ Depth = 400 cm

Convert the depth from centimeters to meters:

1 meter = 100 centimeters

Therefore, 400 cm = 400 / 100 = 4 meters

**The depth of water in the tank is 4 meters.**

questions.question: The smallest four-digit number that is exactly divisible by each of 24, 40 and 56 is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

We need to find the smallest four-digit number that is exactly divisible by 24, 40, and 56.

**Formula Used:**

Smallest number divisible by all given numbers = LCM of the numbers

**Calculation:**

First, find the LCM of 24, 40, and 56.

Prime factorization of 24 = 2³ × 3

Prime factorization of 40 = 2³ × 5

Prime factorization of 56 = 2³ × 7

LCM = 2³ × 3 × 5 × 7

LCM = 8 × 3 × 5 × 7

LCM = 840

So, the smallest 4-digit number which is divisible by 24, 40 and 56 will be a multiple of 840.

Thus, required number = 840 × 2 = 1680

**∴ The correct answer is option 2.**

questions.question: If 6 men and 8 boys can do a piece of work in 10 days while 26 men and 48 boys can do the same in 2 days, the time taken by 15 men and 20 boys in doing the same type of work will be:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Notice the proportional relationship between the given and asked workforce.

Asked workforce: (15 men + 20 boys) = 2.5 × (6 men + 8 boys).

Since the workforce efficiency becomes 2.5 times, the time taken will be divided by 2.5.

Time taken = 10 ÷ 2.5 = 4 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 4 days.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

6 men and 8 boys complete the work in 10 days.

26 men and 48 boys complete the work in 2 days.

**Method Used:**

Total Work = LCM of Days. Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Days.

 
 

 **Person**
 **Days**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 6M + 8B
 10
 10
 1
 
 

 26M + 48B
 2
 5
 
 

⇒ Let efficiency of a man be M and a boy be B.

⇒ 6M + 8B = 1 . . . (i)

⇒ 26M + 48B = 5 . . . (ii)

⇒ Multiplying equation (i) by 6, we get: 36M + 48B = 6 . . . (iii)

⇒ Subtracting (ii) from (iii): 10M = 1 ⇒ M = 0.1

⇒ Substituting M = 0.1 in (i): 6(0.1) + 8B = 1 ⇒ 0.6 + 8B = 1 ⇒ 8B = 0.4 ⇒ B = 0.05

⇒ Efficiency of 15 men and 20 boys = 15M + 20B = 15(0.1) + 20(0.05) = 1.5 + 1.0 = 2.5

⇒ Time taken = Total Work ÷ Efficiency = 10 ÷ 2.5 = 4 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 4 days.**

__
 
• Regeneration is the ability of a fully differentiated organism to give rise to new individuals from their body parts.
 
• This process is common in certain species such as starfish, planarians, and some amphibians.

• This biological process is crucial for healing and recovery from injuries in organisms capable of regeneration.

• This method is common in algae, fungi, and some invertebrates.
 
 
 
• **Fission**
 
 
• It is a type of asexual reproduction where a single organism divides into two or more separate organisms.
 
• Bacteria and protists commonly reproduce through binary fission.
 
 
 
• **Budding**
 
 
• In budding, a new organism develops from an outgrowth or bud due to cell division at one particular site.
 
• Hydra and yeast are examples of organisms that reproduce through budding.

questions.question: A fraction becomes (1)/(2) if 2 is added to the numerator and 5 is added to the denominator. It also becomes (1)/(3) if 2 is subtracted from both the numerator and denominator. The positive difference between the denominator and the numerator of the fraction is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A fraction becomes (1)/(2) if 2 is added to the numerator and 5 is added to the denominator.

It also becomes (1)/(3) if 2 is subtracted from both the numerator and denominator.

Calculation:

1. (x+2)/(y+5) = (1)/(2)

2. (x-2)/(y-2) = (1)/(3)

From equation 1:

 (x+2)/(y+5) = (1)/(2) 

⇒ 2(x + 2) = y + 5

⇒ 2x + 4 = y + 5

⇒ y = 2x - 1 ... (i)

From equation 2:

 (x-2)/(y-2) = (1)/(3) 

⇒ 3(x - 2) = y - 2

⇒ 3x - 6 = y - 2

⇒ y = 3x - 4 ... (ii)

Equating equations (i) and (ii):

2x - 1 = 3x - 4

⇒ 3 = x

Substitute x = 3 in equation (i):

y = 2(3) - 1

⇒ y = 5

The positive difference between the denominator and the numerator is:

|y - x| = |5 - 3| = 2

**The positive difference between the denominator and the numerator of the fraction is 2.**

questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the original cost of 1 pen be x and 1 pencil be y.

New cost of 2 pens and 3 pencils = 2(x − 1.50) + 3(y + 1)

New cost = 2x − 3 + 3y + 3 = 2x + 3y

Notice that the new cost (2x + 3y) exactly equals the original cost of 2 pens and 3 pencils.

Given the new cost is ₹48, the original cost must also be ₹48.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹48.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Cost of 12 pens and 7 pencils = ₹233

Cost of 2 pens and 3 pencils = ₹48 (when pen price drops by ₹1.50 and pencil price rises by ₹1)

**Calculation:**

Let the original cost of a pen be x and a pencil be y.

⇒ 12x + 7y = 233 ... (1)

According to the second condition:

⇒ 2(x − 1.50) + 3(y + 1) = 48

⇒ 2x − 3 + 3y + 3 = 48

⇒ 2x + 3y = 48

⇒ 2x = 48 − 3y

⇒ x = 24 − 1.5y ... (2)

Substitute equation (2) into equation (1):

⇒ 12(24 − 1.5y) + 7y = 233

⇒ 288 − 18y + 7y = 233

⇒ 288 − 11y = 233

⇒ 11y = 288 − 233

⇒ 11y = 55

⇒ y = 5

Substitute y = 5 in equation (2):

⇒ x = 24 − 1.5 × 5

⇒ x = 24 − 7.5 = 16.5

The original cost of 2 pens and 3 pencils:

⇒ 2x + 3y = 2 × 16.5 + 3 × 5

⇒ 33 + 15 = 48

**∴ The correct answer is ₹48.**

questions.question: Cells of the meristematic tissue are very active, but they lack:
questions.solution:

__
 
• Meristematic tissue cells are highly active and are involved in continuous cell division.
 
• These cells possess a dense cytoplasm which supports their high metabolic activity.
 
• The cells have thin cellulose walls that provide flexibility and support for cell division.
 
• Meristematic cells contain prominent nuclei which are essential for regulating cell division and growth.
 
• These cells generally lack vacuoles or have very small vacuoles because vacuoles are more prominent in mature cells and are involved in storage and maintenance of cell turgor.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Parenchyma Cells**

 
 
• These are the most common type of plant cells and are found in various parts of the plant.
 
• They have thin cell walls and large central vacuoles.
 
• Parenchyma cells are involved in storage, photosynthesis, and tissue repair.
 
 
 
• **Collenchyma Cells**
 
 
• These cells provide structural support to growing parts of the plant.
 
• They have thicker cell walls compared to parenchyma cells and are typically found in stems and leaves.
 
 
 
• **Sclerenchyma Cells**
 
 
• These cells are known for their thick, lignified cell walls which provide mechanical support.
 
• Sclerenchyma cells are found in non-growing regions of the plant such as the bark and mature stems.

questions.question: Which of the following products are formed when sodium sulphate reacts with barium chloride?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**White precipitate of BaSO₄ and 2NaCl (aq)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• When sodium sulphate reacts with barium chloride, the reaction produces barium sulphate (BaSO₄) and sodium chloride (NaCl).
 
• Barium sulphate is a white precipitate that forms as a result of this reaction.
 
• The balanced chemical equation for this reaction is Na₂SO₄ + BaCl₂ → BaSO₄ + 2NaCl.
 
• This reaction is a typical example of a double displacement reaction.
 
• In a double displacement reaction, the ions of the reactants exchange places to form new compounds.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Solubility Rules**

 
 
• Barium sulphate is insoluble in water, which is why it forms a precipitate.
 
• Sodium chloride is soluble in water and remains in the aqueous solution.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Barium Sulphate**
 
 
• Barium sulphate is used in medical imaging as a radiocontrast agent for X-ray imaging and other diagnostic procedures.
 
• It is also used in the production of paints, coatings, and plastics.
 
 
 
• **Double Displacement Reactions**
 
 
• These reactions are also known as metathesis reactions.
 
• They typically occur in aqueous solutions where the ions can move freely and react with each other.

questions.question: Which of the following is the SI unit of work done?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Joule**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The SI unit of work done is the **Joule** (J).
 
• A Joule is defined as the amount of work done when a force of one newton displaces an object by one meter in the direction of the force.
 
• It is a derived unit in the International System of Units (SI).
 
• The unit is named after the English physicist **James Prescott Joule**.
 
• Work done can also be represented in other units such as ergs, but Joule is the standard SI unit.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Erg**

 
 
• It is a unit of work or energy in the CGS (centimeter-gram-second) system.
 
• 1 Joule is equal to 10⁷ ergs.
 
 
 
• **Newton**
 
 
• It is the SI unit of force.
 
• 1 Newton is the force required to accelerate a mass of one kilogram by one meter per second squared.
 
 
 
• **Metre**
 
 
• It is the SI unit of length.
 
• One meter is the distance light travels in a vacuum in 1/299,792,458 seconds.

questions.question: In the case of reflection of light from a concave mirror, when a parallel beam of light is incident on the reflecting surface, reflected light ________.

options.text: appears to converge at the centre of curvature
appears to diverge from the principal focus
appears to diverge from the centre of curvature
appears to converge at the principal focus

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**appears to converge at the principal focus**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• When a parallel beam of light is incident on a concave mirror, it reflects and converges at a single point called the principal focus.
 
• The principal focus of a concave mirror is the point where parallel rays of light meet after reflection.
 
• The distance between the mirror's surface and the principal focus is known as the focal length.
 
• The center of curvature is the center of the sphere from which the concave mirror segment is taken.
 
• The principal axis is the line that passes through the center of curvature and the midpoint of the mirror.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Convex Mirror**

 
 
• A convex mirror diverges parallel beams of light, making them appear to originate from a point behind the mirror called the virtual focus.
 
• Convex mirrors are used in vehicles as rear-view mirrors due to their wider field of view.
 
 
 
• **Reflection Laws**
 
 
• The angle of incidence is equal to the angle of reflection.
 
• The incident ray, the reflected ray, and the normal to the surface all lie in the same plane.
 
 
 
• **Uses of Concave Mirrors**
 
 
• Concave mirrors are used in telescopes to gather and focus light.
 
• They are also used in headlights of vehicles to focus light beams into parallel rays.

questions.question: What percentage of solar energy is captured by green plants in terrestrial ecosystem?
questions.solution:

__
 
• Green plants in terrestrial ecosystems capture only about **1 percent** of the solar energy that reaches them.
 
• This energy is utilized for the process of **photosynthesis**, where it is converted into chemical energy.
 
• The chemical energy is stored in the form of **glucose** and other organic molecules.
 
• The efficiency of solar energy capture by plants is relatively low due to various factors such as **reflection, transmission, and absorption of light** by non-photosynthetic parts.
 
• Despite the low percentage, this energy forms the base of the **food chain** in terrestrial ecosystems, supporting a wide range of life forms.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Photosynthesis**

 
 
• It is the process by which green plants, algae, and some bacteria convert light energy into chemical energy.
 
• Photosynthesis primarily occurs in the **chloroplasts** of plant cells.
 
 
 
• **Energy Transfer in Ecosystems**
 
 
• Energy captured by plants is transferred to herbivores when they consume plants, and subsequently to carnivores when they consume herbivores.
 
• Only about **10 percent** of the energy is transferred from one trophic level to the next.
 
 
 
• **Solar Energy Utilization**
 
 
• A large portion of solar energy is not used for photosynthesis and is instead reflected or absorbed as heat.
 
• Plants have evolved various adaptations to maximize their **light absorption efficiency**.

questions.question: A thief running at a speed of 8 km/h is chased by a policeman whose speed is 10 km/h. If the thief is 100 m ahead of the policeman, then the time required for the policeman to catch the thief will be:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Relative speed of policeman = 10 − 8 = 2 km/h

Distance gap to close = 100 m = 0.1 km

Time required = Distance ÷ Relative speed = 0.1 ÷ 2 = 1/20 hours

Time in minutes = 1/20 × 60 = 3 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 3 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed of the policeman (Sₚ) = 10 km/h

Speed of the thief (Sₜ) = 8 km/h

Initial distance ahead (D) = 100 m = 0.1 km

**Formula Used:**

Relative Speed = Sₚ − Sₜ (Since they move in the same direction)

Time = Distance ÷ Relative Speed

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e608d9911945b0b381ea958572edfa19dc2c6160b6bab924db96c7070f4db41a.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Relative Speed = 10 − 8 = 2 km/h

⇒ Time required to catch the thief = 0.1 km ÷ 2 km/h = 0.05 hours

⇒ To convert hours into minutes, multiply by 60:

⇒ Time required = 0.05 × 60 = 3 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 3 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed (Same Direction)

When two bodies move in the same direction at speeds S₁ and S₂ (where S₁ > S₂), their relative speed is S₁ − S₂.

Relative Speed (Opposite Direction)

When two bodies move towards each other at speeds S₁ and S₂, their relative speed is S₁ + S₂.

• In this process, chlorine gas is also produced at the anode as a by-product.
 
 
 
• **Other Extraction Methods**
 
 
• Metals like zinc and iron are extracted from their ores by reduction using carbon or carbon monoxide.
 
• Lead is typically extracted by roasting its sulfide ore followed by reduction.

questions.question: A solution contains 25 g of copper chloride salt in 250 g of water. Calculate the concentration in terms of mass by mass percentage of the solution.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A solution contains 25 g of copper chloride salt in 250 g of water.

**Concept:**

Mass by mass percentage concentration is defined as the mass of solute divided by the total mass of solution, multiplied by 100.

**Formula Used:**

Mass percentage = (Mass of solute / Total mass of solution) × 100

**Calculation:**

⇒ Mass of solute (copper chloride) = 25 g

⇒ Mass of solvent (water) = 250 g

⇒ Total mass of solution = Mass of solute + Mass of solvent

⇒ Total mass of solution = 25 g + 250 g = 275 g

⇒ Mass percentage = (25 g / 275 g) × 100

⇒ Mass percentage = 0.0909 × 100

⇒ Mass percentage = 9.09%

**∴ The correct answer is option 1: 0.0909**

questions.question: Which of the following fractions is greater than (2)/(3) and less than (4)/(5) ?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

We need to find a fraction greater than 2/3 and less than 4/5.

Calculation:

2/3 ≈ 0.6667 and 4/5 = 0.8

Option 1: 3/4 = 0.75

Option 2: 1/2 = 0.5

Option 3: 5/6 ≈ 0.8333

Option 4: 9/11 ≈ 0.8182

Check each option:

Option 1: 0.75 lies between 0.6667 and 0.8. Correct

Option 2: 0.5 is less than 0.6667. Wrong

Option 3: 0.8333 is greater than 0.8. Wrong

Option 4: 0.8182 is greater than 0.8. Wrong

**∴ The fraction 3/4 (Option 1) is greater than 2/3 and less than 4/5.**
